bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.issue_description / staged vulnerable source snapshot / saved sanitizer trace
bug_description.normalized: When the staged malformed XCF is decoded, the crashing `loadLayer()` invocation parses a visible RGB layer and `composeTiles()` allocates RGB32 `QImage` backing stores for its non-zero tile grid. On the witnessed path, `loadHierarchy()` then reads its hierarchy header from file offset 0: the saved RGB warning's bogus `bpp` value `543582572` matches bytes 8-11 of the 66-byte PoC, and the same header yields a hierarchy-local `offset` of `1694498816`. `loadHierarchy()` scans the level-offset table until the terminating 0, saves `pos()==32`, and then calls `xcf_io.device()->seek(offset)`. In the staged Qt source, `QBuffer::seek()` rejects that out-of-range position and returns false without moving the cursor, so `loadLevel()` reads from the unchanged post-scan cursor instead of from offset `1694498816`; bytes 32-43 decode there as `width=21`, `height=16`, `offset=0`. The vulnerable `if (offset == 0) return true;` branch treats that zero tile-data offset as success and returns without calling `loadTileRLE()`, `layer.assignBytes()`, or otherwise clearing the already allocated tiles. Because an earlier visible layer has already initialized `xcf_image.image`, `loadLayer()` takes the merge path, and `mergeLayerIntoImage()` hands the untouched tile to `QPainter::drawImage()`. Qt's paint pipeline then reads from that never-initialized source tile and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in `destStoreMonoLsb`.

source.description: Current-layer header materialization. The crashing `loadLayer()` invocation first decodes the attacker-controlled layer dimensions and type that later determine tile allocation and the RGB merge path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 66-byte GIMP XCF blob beginning with `gimp xcf file\0`; `file(1)` also identifies it as GIMP XCF image data. In the crashing `loadLayer()` call, bytes from this blob are decoded here, and the saved warning `Found layer of type RGB but with bpp != 3 543582572` confirms the parsed layer type is `RGB_GIMAGE`.
source.note: This is the first project-side statement in the crashing layer that turns the XCF bytes into the specific layer state later consumed by `composeTiles()` and `mergeLayerIntoImage()`.

sink.description: Project sink. `QPainter::drawImage()` receives the current layer tile as a source image even though the tile backing store was never initialized on the `offset == 0` path.
sink.note: The saved MSAN stack runs directly below this call through `QRasterPaintEngine::drawImage`, `fillRect_normalized`, and `blend_untransformed_generic` before crashing in `destStoreMonoLsb`, so this line is the project handoff that exposes the undefined tile bytes to the Qt paint pipeline.

root_cause.description: Missing tile initialization on the `offset == 0` success path. The function accepts a top-level level with no tile-data offset and returns without defining the already allocated tile pixels.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` changes exactly this branch to fill every allocated tile with `Qt::transparent` before returning, preventing later reads from uninitialized `QImage` backing stores.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN origin. `composeTiles()` allocates the RGB tile `QImage` backing store whose pixels later remain unwritten on the `offset == 0` path.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved sanitizer trace attributes the uninitialized bytes to the heap allocation chain `__interceptor_malloc` -> `QImageData::create` -> `QImage::QImage` -> `XCFImageFormat::composeTiles`.

coarse_trace.summary: The crashing layer header is decoded from attacker-controlled XCF bytes, and `composeTiles()` derives a non-zero tile grid and allocates RGB tile `QImage` backing stores.

On the witnessed RGB-layer path, `loadHierarchy()` reads its header from file offset 0, corrects the bogus RGB `bpp`, scans the level-offset table until the terminating 0, saves `pos()==32`, then attempts `seek(1694498816)`; `QBuffer::seek()` rejects that position and leaves the cursor unchanged, so `loadLevel()` reads `width=21`, `height=16`, and `offset=0` from the unchanged post-scan cursor.
The vulnerable `offset == 0` branch returns success without decoding or clearing any tile pixels, leaving the already allocated `image_tiles` storage uninitialized.
Because an earlier visible layer already initialized `xcf_image.image`, the current layer is merged rather than copied, and `mergeLayerIntoImage()` receives the untouched tile set.
The RGB fast path calls `QPainter::drawImage()` on the never-filled tile, and the saved Qt/MSAN stack consumes those undefined bytes in `destStoreMonoLsb`.

fine_trace.note: Parses the current layer header from attacker-controlled XCF bytes. On the crashing invocation, the later warning `Found layer of type RGB but with bpp != 3 543582572` shows this layer's parsed type is `RGB_GIMAGE`; because the later sink iterates and draws at least one tile, the parsed dimensions yield a non-zero tile grid on the witnessed path.

Materializes the tile grid from the parsed layer dimensions. These counts are non-zero on the witnessed path, so this layer owns at least one tile slot that must be filled before any later merge reads it.

For RGB layers, each tile slot gets a heap-allocated `QImage` backing store. The saved MSAN origin stack points here through `QImageData::create`; the pixel bytes stay undefined until later tile decoding writes them.

`loadLayer()` materializes the hierarchy and mask offsets for the crashing layer. Reaching this read also proves the layer did not take the earlier `if (layer.visible == 0) return true;` exit at lines 588-590, without needing to claim whether `layer.visible` came from `PROP_VISIBLE` or from previously retained/default state.

Before calling `loadHierarchy()`, `loadLayer()` uses the attacker-controlled `layer.hierarchy_offset` in a `seek()` attempt. The trace does not assume that attempt succeeded; the next step anchors the actual hierarchy-header read location from the witnessed bytes and warning.

On the witnessed RGB-layer path, this hierarchy header is read from file offset 0: the saved warning `Found layer of type RGB but with bpp != 3 543582572` matches bytes 8-11 of the 66-byte PoC, so the same read also supplies the hierarchy-local `offset` value `1694498816` from bytes 12-15. The switch then corrects the bogus `bpp` to 3 for the RGB layer before continuing.

Just above this line, `loadHierarchy()` scans 4-byte level-offset entries until the terminating 0. For the witness, that scan consumes bytes 16-31 of the PoC and leaves `saved_pos == 32`, which is the post-scan cursor value later restored or reused.

`loadHierarchy()` then attempts `seek(1694498816)`. In the staged Qt source, `QBuffer::seek()` treats positions past the buffer size as invalid, logs `QBuffer::seek: Invalid pos: 1694498816`, returns false, and leaves the cursor at `saved_pos` instead of moving it to `offset`.

Because step 8 left the cursor unchanged at file offset 32, `loadLevel()` reads the level header from bytes 32-43 of the PoC rather than from `1694498816`. Those bytes decode to `width = 21`, `height = 16`, and a tile-data `offset = 0`.

Root cause. Even though step 2 produced a non-zero tile grid and step 3 already allocated tile backing stores, this branch treats the zero tile-data offset from step 9 as success and returns before the tile loops run. Neither `loadTileRLE()` nor `layer.assignBytes()` writes any pixel data, so the allocated `QImage` tiles remain uninitialized.

The saved crash stack reaches `mergeLayerIntoImage()` from line 641, so this layer is not the first visible layer: `xcf_image.initialized` is already true from an earlier visible layer, and the current layer is merged into the existing destination image instead of copied. That control decision exposes the untouched current-layer tiles to merge code.

Sink. This line is inside the fast-path body at lines 1874-1880, so its execution is the reachability evidence that that guard evaluated true on the witnessed path; the trace does not need a separate producer step for `layer.apply_mask`. `QPainter::drawImage()` hands the never-written tile `QImage` to Qt, and the saved stack immediately descends through `QRasterPaintEngine::drawImage`, `fillRect_normalized`, and `blend_untransformed_generic` before MSAN reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in `destStoreMonoLsb`.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is a 66-byte GIMP XCF image beginning with `gimp xcf file\0`. On the saved vulnerable run, the crashing `loadLayer()` invocation reaches a visible RGB layer and `composeTiles()` allocates RGB32 tile images for a non-zero tile grid. On that same path, `loadHierarchy()` reads its header from file offset 0, the saved RGB warning reveals that its bogus `bpp` came from bytes 8-11 of the PoC, it scans level-offset entries until `pos()==32`, and `QBuffer::seek(1694498816)` then fails without moving the cursor. `loadLevel()` therefore decodes `width=21`, `height=16`, and a tile-data `offset=0` from bytes 32-43. The function returns success without decoding or clearing those tiles, and because `xcf_image.initialized` is already true from an earlier visible layer, `mergeLayerIntoImage()` passes the untouched tile to `QPainter::drawImage()`, which crashes in the saved Qt `destStoreMonoLsb` path.

format.name: XCF
format.contract: A GIMP XCF image accepted by `readXCF()` that, on the crashing layer, reaches a visible RGB layer with a non-zero tile grid and then causes `loadHierarchy()` to read its hierarchy header from file offset 0, scan level-offset entries until `saved_pos == 32`, fail `QBuffer::seek(1694498816)` without changing the cursor, and consequently make `loadLevel()` decode `width=21`, `height=16`, and a tile-data `offset=0` from bytes 32-43 of the same witness while `xcf_image.initialized` is already true. On the witnessed path, `loadLevel()` returns success without calling `loadTileRLE()` or `layer.assignBytes()`, and `mergeLayerIntoImage()` then executes `painter.drawImage(...)` on the untouched `image_tiles` entry. The staged evidence establishes this exact failed-seek/post-scan-cursor shape, not a broader class of malformed XCF files.
